correctness.rationale: The OR flag is Bernoulli with no-detection probability u_t. Its information and unbiased estimator variance follow by exact algebra. For every interior occupancy, information per visit tends to zero as t increases; the sharp phase follows from the boundary score (b²/a)^t/t and a uniform upper bound in the bounded regime. In the divergent regime H_t is uniformly equivalent to t(epsilon exp(mu t)+exp(-nu t)) and has a coercive two-tail minimum within O(1) of log(1/epsilon)/lambda. A uniform local expansion proves the lattice periodic factor. For full histories the exact boundary chi-squared information is K^t-1 and for interior occupancy the complete-data information bound guarantees finite t; these yield divergence for all p>f. The embedded checker independently reconstructs exact finite likelihoods and passes 191 assertions; the infinite claims are analytical, not extrapolated from tests.

originality.rationale: The inspected pre-2017 primary occupancy-design literature establishes two-sided detection error, study-design tradeoffs, and numerical repeat-visit optimization, but not the claimed exact near-ubiquity dichotomy p>2f-f², its integer-lattice asymptotic, or the proved contrast with full retained histories. Later aggregation research supplies general mixture/aggregation foundations without a located exact near-ubiquity phase theorem. This is a best-knowledge originality assessment, not an independent historical-priority certificate. A highly plausible 1985 predecessor was abstract-only and remains explicitly at risk.
residual_risks: McClish–Quade (1985) is exceptionally close in model and scientific objective; full text was inaccessible. A hidden exact integer near-one phase in it or its descendants would invalidate novelty.
The general repeated-test prevalence and diagnostic-testing literature is broader than the inspected sources, so historical priority is not independently certified.
Some general full-history Fisher-information facts are routine and not asserted as separate original contributions.

value.rationale: Repeated occupancy visits and false sightings are genuine ecological survey-design problems. The new result identifies a sharp detection-quality condition under which reporting only whether a site was ever detected fundamentally changes the growth order of the optimal number of revisit attempts as occupied sites become nearly universal. The logarithmic design rate and its integer-lattice correction quantify the value of retaining histories, rather than merely reexpressing a binomial variance. The result is restricted to known calibrated rates and ideal unit-cost visits, and has relevance as a model benchmark rather than unconditional field guidance.
